solutions.check: bars rebuilt from the blog's numbered answers (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Sorted out wordplay — one part

blocks.note: a pun is play on words
the Roman numeral for one
a shed is a parting in the hair, a Scots and dialect sense

explanation.surface: Someone untangles a piece of wordplay, at least one part of it.
explanation.walkthrough: SHED for a parting of the hair is an old word found in Chambers, a favourite source for Mephisto.
explanation.definitionFit: To sort someone out can mean to deal with them severely, which is to discipline or chastise them.

clue.text: Written report for boss reveals openings for best candidates

indicators.note: to boss is a slang verb meaning to bungle or botch, so the letters are messed up
openings are the starting letters of the following words

blocks.note: pro is Latin for for, as in pros and cons
taken as written, to be jumbled
the opening letter of best
the opening letter of candidates

explanation.surface: A written report for the boss reveals the strongest applicants for a job.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Boss' looks like the report's reader but is a verb meaning to bungle, the anagram signal for REVEALS plus B and C.
explanation.definitionFit: A procès-verbal is a French term for an official written record or minutes of proceedings.

clue.text: Curt expression of admiration for Macbeth’s crowns?

indicators.note: curt means cut short, so the phrase loses its final letter

blocks.note: 'No less!' is an exclamation of being impressed

explanation.surface: A clipped word of praise is offered for the crowns worn by Macbeth.
explanation.walkthrough: 'No less!' cut short gives NOLES; the question mark warns that 'crowns' means heads, not regalia.
explanation.definitionFit: Nole is a Shakespearean word for the head, the crown of the skull, so Macbeth's era would call heads noles.

clue.text: Old royalty, Henry having money

blocks.note: the Incas were the ruling dynasty of ancient Peru
H is the symbol for the henry, the unit of inductance

explanation.surface: An old king named Henry is pictured as being rich.
explanation.definitionFit: To be in cash is an idiom for being well supplied with funds, the state of being flush.

clue.text: Shocked feeling cold in narrow boat

indicators.note: in places one item inside another, here within the boat

blocks.note: a sandal is a long narrow boat used on the Barbary coast
C is the abbreviation for cold on taps

explanation.surface: Someone feels shocked and chilly while aboard a canal narrowboat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Narrow boat' suggests a British canal barge, but the boat here is the obscure sandal.
explanation.definitionFit: Scandal is moral outrage, the indignant feeling caused by something disgraceful.

clue.text: Harrow and others wanting to back Eton’s head

indicators.note: wanting means lacking, so the following little word is taken away
the head of a word is its first letter
to back means to come behind, so this letter goes at the end

blocks.note: taken as written
the first letter of Eton

explanation.surface: Harrow and other schools want to support the head of their rival Eton.
explanation.walkthrough: OTHERS without T and O leaves HERS. Harrow and Eton are famous English private schools, which makes 'Harrow' look like a proper noun.
explanation.definitionFit: A herse is a harrow, both the farm implement and the spiked portcullis of a castle gateway.

clue.text: Nut with iron fist’s first to accept owning surrender

indicators.note: the first of a word is its opening letter
to accept is to take in, so the preceding letters enclose the next word

blocks.note: a nut is an en, the printing measure
Fe is the chemical symbol for iron
of means belonging to, as in the house of my father
the opening letter of fist

explanation.surface: A tough nut with an iron fist has to accept giving in.
explanation.walkthrough: In printing, an en space is nicknamed a nut, and 'iron fist' looks like one phrase but splits into two pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: To enfeoff is to hand over a fief or estate to another, a formal surrender of feudal land.

clue.text: Woolly mass, a lot of sheep en masse?

indicators.note: a lot of means most but not all, so the last letter is dropped

blocks.note: a group of sheep together is a flock

explanation.surface: A fluffy cloud of wool, rather like a crowd of sheep packed together.
explanation.definitionFit: A floc is a loose fluffy clump of particles, a tuft or woolly aggregate formed in a liquid.

clue.text: Part of journal in gobbledygook jargon

indicators.note: part of tells us the letters are a piece of the words that follow

blocks.note: running across the end of journal, in, and the start of gobbledygook

explanation.surface: A section of an academic journal written in impenetrable jargon.
explanation.definitionFit: Lingo is informal for a specialised vocabulary, the jargon of a profession or group.

clue.text: It’s flipping irksome accommodating constant Australian boorishness

indicators.note: flipping suggests tossing something over, so the letters are thrown about
accommodating means giving room to, so the word takes in a letter

blocks.note: taken as written
c is the symbol for a constant, such as the speed of light

explanation.surface: Someone complains that loutish Aussie behaviour is flipping annoying.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Flipping' reads as a mild British swearword, but it is the anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: An ocker is a loud uncultivated Australian, so ockerism is the brash loutish behaviour of such a man.

clue.text: Media put out in characteristic masterstroke

indicators.note: put out means disturbed, so the media letters are knocked into a new order
in places the jumbled letters inside the next word

blocks.note: taken as written, to be rearranged
core as an adjective means central and essential, as in core values

explanation.surface: The press is unsettled by a typically brilliant move.
explanation.definitionFit: Coup de maître is French for a master's stroke, a brilliant decisive move.

clue.text: College directed towards energy provider largely with a common focus

indicators.note: largely means mostly, so the company name loses its last letter

blocks.note: C is a standard abbreviation for college
on can mean aimed at, as in an attack on
Centrica is the British energy company that owns British Gas

explanation.surface: A college is pointed towards an energy supplier, with everyone sharing one aim.
explanation.walkthrough: Centrica is a big UK gas and electricity supplier, the owner of British Gas.
explanation.definitionFit: Concentric circles share one centre, so a common centre point or focus is the geometric sense.

clue.text: Pope more abrupt spurning outsiders

indicators.note: spurning outsiders means rejecting the letters at either end of the word

blocks.note: gruffer means curter, more brusque

explanation.surface: A Pope becomes curter and shuns those outside the Church.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pope' looks like the pontiff but is a small freshwater fish.
explanation.definitionFit: The ruffe is a small perch-like freshwater fish whose old common name is the pope.

clue.text: Member of parliament about to take night tram

blocks.note: a group of owls is called a parliament
ca is short for circa, about
R stands for recipe, Latin for take, on prescriptions

explanation.surface: An MP is about to catch the late-night tram home.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Member of parliament' reads as an MP but is a bird, since owls gather in a parliament.
explanation.definitionFit: An owl car is an American term for a streetcar that runs through the late hours, like a nocturnal bird.

clue.text: Young blood rebuffed title of respect for Malayan prince

indicators.note: rebuffed suggests being pushed back, so the word is read in the other direction

blocks.note: a knut is an Edwardian dandy, a young man about town
U is a Burmese title of respect, as in U Thant

explanation.surface: A young aristocrat is snubbed when he tries to address a Malay prince respectfully.
explanation.definitionFit: Tunku is a Malay royal title borne by princes, as with Tunku Abdul Rahman.

clue.text: The solution to this you knew finally yielded “scavenger”

blocks.clueFragment: The solution to this you knew finally yielded “scavenger”
blocks.note: surface reading: a solver finally cracks the clue and the answer turns out to be a scavenger
setter's reading: the answer is itself a solution, a cleaning liquid, and also an old name for a street sweeper

explanation.surface: A solver who has worked it out at last finds the answer is a scavenger.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Solution' is a pun: the answer of a clue and a cleaning fluid.
explanation.definitionFit: A scavenger was once a person employed to clean the streets, one who removes dirt and filth.

clue.text: Substance sickly and ultimately syrupy

indicators.note: sickly suggests something unwell and out of shape, so the next word is scrambled
ultimately points to the final letter of the next word

blocks.note: quid is an old word for the substance or essence of a thing, as in quiddity
taken as written, to be rearranged
the final letter of syrupy

explanation.surface: A cloyingly sweet, syrupy substance is described.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue also describes the answer, a sweet sticky preserve.
explanation.definitionFit: Quiddany is an old thick quince syrup or jelly, a sugary preserve fairly called a sickly syrupy substance.

clue.text: Focus perhaps on neat footwear

indicators.note: in an across answer, one thing on another comes after it

blocks.note: neat is an old word for cattle, so an ox
the Focus is a car model made by Ford

explanation.surface: Someone concentrates on smart, tidy shoes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Focus' looks like a verb of attention, but it is a Ford car, and 'neat' means cattle, not tidy.
explanation.definitionFit: Oxfords are classic lace-up leather shoes, a style of formal footwear.

clue.text: Had to renounce God with replacement prayer beads

indicators.note: to renounce is to give something up, so a letter is removed

blocks.note: a sub is a substitute, a replacement player
taken as written
D is the abbreviation for Deus, Latin for God

explanation.surface: Someone had to give up their faith and take up a substitute set of prayer beads.
explanation.definitionFit: A subha is a Muslim rosary, a string of beads used to count prayers.

clue.text: Black capturing a rook getting material

indicators.note: capturing means taking prisoner, so one word holds the others inside

blocks.note: jet is a deep glossy black
taken as written
to rook someone is to swindle them, a con

explanation.surface: In chess, Black takes a rook and gains material.
explanation.walkthrough: In chess 'material' means pieces won, so the surface is a game report.
explanation.definitionFit: Jaconet is a light cotton fabric, so it is cloth or material.

clue.text: Set foot on spiritual enchanting place of old

indicators.note: set on means placed in front, so this letter leads

blocks.note: f is an abbreviation for foot
aerie, or aery, means ethereal or incorporeal

explanation.surface: Someone steps onto holy ground at a magical place of long ago.
explanation.definitionFit: Faerie is the archaic name for fairyland, the magical realm of fairies in old romance.

clue.text: Italian monopoly to dismay tax officer

blocks.note: to appal is to fill with horror or dismay
TO is short for tax officer

explanation.surface: An Italian state monopoly is said to dismay the taxman.
explanation.definitionFit: An appalto is an Italian term for a contract or monopoly granted by the state, such as for tobacco or salt.

clue.text: Adult comic’s associated with dog, not the black dog

indicators.note: not the black tells us to drop the letter standing for black

blocks.note: Viz is a British comic magazine with crude adult humour, plus the 's
a lab is a Labrador retriever

explanation.surface: A comedian with adult material is linked to a dog, but not the black one.
explanation.walkthrough: VIZ is a British comic famous for rude humour, and 'black dog' hints at depression rather than a pet.
explanation.definitionFit: The vizsla is a Hungarian hunting breed, a sleek russet pointer.

clue.text: Gibe cut old Queen

blocks.note: snee is an obsolete dialect word for cut
R is short for regina, queen

explanation.surface: A jeer is aimed at a former queen.
explanation.definitionFit: A sneer is a scornful remark or expression, much like a taunt or jeer.

clue.text: Spam left out getting mould as before

blocks.note: taken as written
L is the abbreviation for left

explanation.surface: Spam left out goes mouldy, just as it did before.

explanation.definitionFit: Plasm once meant a mould or matrix in which something is cast or shaped, an old sense now obsolete.

clue.text: Essential ingredient for sherlocks — correspondence’s covering in dust?

setter's reading: metal filings used as fingerprint powder, with mail punning on letters and on chain armour

explanation.surface: A detective's key tool is a dusting of letters for fingerprints.
explanation.walkthrough: Fingerprint powder can be iron filings dusted on with a magnet, so the dust a detective needs is a word ending in MAIL.
explanation.definitionFit: Limail is metal filings, fine particles of iron, effectively a metallic powder or dust.

clue.text: Nice cover of dance hit in the style of Shangri-Las?

hit suggests being knocked about, so the letters are reorganised

blocks.note: taken as written
the first and last letters of dance

explanation.surface: A pleasing cover version of a dance hit, sung like the Shangri-Las girl group.
explanation.walkthrough: The Shangri-Las were a 1960s girl group, but Shangri-La is a fabled paradise.
explanation.definitionFit: Edenic means like Eden, paradisal, and Shangri-La is a mythical earthly paradise.

clue.text: Cruel person reverting back to Mephistophelean work

the back of a word is its final letter

blocks.note: an ogre is a brutal, cruel person
the last letter of Mephistophelean

explanation.walkthrough: The surface nods to the puzzle's own name, Mephisto.
explanation.definitionFit: Ergon is Greek for work, a task or function, used in English as a term for a deed.

clue.text: Unarmed marine avoiding a shot

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written, the letter removed

explanation.walkthrough: 'Shot' suggests gunfire, fitting a marine, but signals the anagram.
explanation.definitionFit: Inerm is a botanical term for lacking thorns or spines, hence without weapons or defences.

clue.text: US behind news breaking foreseeing calamity?

clue.text: Tips good Italian fashion house to release latest in menswear

the final letter of menswear

blocks.note: taken as written

clue.text: Separate gases break down after splitting atom
